title: Combine endless: recipe-complexity options at run start
body:
Idea from user:

> Option to turn on links for combine: recipes without needs, etc.
>
> I meant, when you start the game you can decide how complex the recipes are.
>
> It means they wouldn't be able to complete the collection but could make gameplay easier for some players.

Rough shape:
- At run start (Combine endless), let the player choose which link types count toward recipes (e.g. drop `n` needs, keep `f`/`w`, etc.).
- Trade-off: easier gameplay, but the run can't contribute to collection completion (discoveries won't unlock, or are flagged separately).
- Open questions:
  - Does score still count toward leaderboards, or is it a separate "assisted" ladder?
  - How to surface the trade-off clearly in the pre-run UI so players know what they're giving up.
  - Interaction with Fast mode (which already drops bands / 2-part only) — is this a third axis or layered onto the same picker?

title: Admin bulk upload: default new items to draft/review, not live
body:
Bulk upload currently lands items as `live` (or close to it). Safer default: new items come in as `draft` or `review` so they can be vetted before going public.

Need to consider dependency chains:
- If item A is uploaded as draft and item B's recipe links to A, what's the status of the link? Does B promote with A still in draft?
- Should promotion to `live` cascade / validate that all referenced items are also live, or at least warn?
- How does this interact with Combine theme membership and reachability — a draft item in a theme would break reachability.

Open:
- Pick default: `draft` (fully hidden) vs `review` (visible to admins, queued).
- Decide if bulk upload should have a per-batch status override.

title: Combine: post-100% experience and "first completed on" milestone

Once a player hits 100% collection, what's left? Framing: the collection is the goal; the leaderboard is the sport. Endless keeps running and score keeps going — that's the long tail.

Add a "first completed on <date>" personal milestone on the account/collection view so hitting 100% feels like a real moment, not just a silently capped counter.

title: User feedback surface: suggest item/recipe, report bugs
body:
Add a user-facing feedback surface that routes to admin review. Categories:

- **Suggest an item** — free-form with context (where they expected to find/use it).
- **Suggest a recipe** — let the user pick the inputs (items the recipe goes into / is made from) via an item picker, plus the proposed output.
- **Something broken / report an issue** — current page/item context attached automatically.
- Generic "other / feedback" bucket.

Shape:
- New `feedback` table (or reuse an existing one) with type, payload JSON, user id (if signed in), url/context, status.
- Admin surface at `/admin/feedback` to triage: dismiss, convert-to-item/recipe draft, respond.
- Rate-limit anonymous submissions; require auth for recipe suggestions (reduce spam).
- Consider PostHog event + email digest to the admin.

Open:
- Should a recipe suggestion auto-create a `draft` recipe record for the admin to review, or stay as free-text until promoted?
- Public credit for accepted suggestions, or private only?

comments.body:
Entry point to add: **icon button on the tile chart / recipe view** so a player can one-tap report "this recipe seems off" with the specific recipe/tile already attached to the payload. That context (recipe id, parent item, tile pair) is far more useful than a free-form "something's wrong" — consider auto-populating the report with:

- recipe id + output item
- tile inputs
- route/url
- user id (if signed in)

So the report category "something broken" grows a sub-type like "recipe looks wrong." Admin triage then has everything needed to jump straight to `/admin/items/[id]` or `/admin/tree` and fix it.

Extension: **inline thumbs up/down reactions on Combine recipes.**

During a Combine run, when a player sees a recipe output, let them react with 👍 / 👎 directly on the result tile (or on the recipe view). Specifically:

- **Disagree (👎) on a recipe** = lightweight structured feedback — "this recipe doesn't feel right." Captures recipe id + user + optional one-tap reason ("too obscure," "wrong output," "missing a step") without opening the full feedback form.
- **Agree (👍)** = positive signal, especially useful once the admin analytics in T-0035 lands (correlate recipe love/hate with usage counts).

Why this is nice:
- Lower friction than "report an issue" — players mid-game won't open a form, but they'll tap a thumb.
- Produces quantitative signal admins can sort by: "recipes with the most 👎 / 👍 ratio" surfaces curation targets fast.
- Complements the icon-button report entry point already in this task — thumbs = quick reaction, icon-button = detailed report.

Shape:
- New `recipe_reactions` table (`recipe_id`, `user_id`, `value`, `reason?`, `created_at`) OR fold into the same `feedback` table with type `recipe_reaction`.
- Rate-limit per user per recipe (one vote, can flip).
- Admin view: recipes sorted by net sentiment, filterable.

Related: T-0035 (admin analytics — reaction ratio is a column there).

Taking this. Scoping to a shippable first slice; deferring the two extensions in comments to child tasks so this one can land.

**In scope (this pass):**
- `feedback` table (`type`, `payload jsonb`, `userId?`, `url`, `status`, timestamps). Migration `0014`.
- `POST /api/feedback` — rate-limited via `limiters.reports`; recipe suggestions require auth.
- `GET` + `PATCH /api/admin/feedback` for triage.
- User surface: a global "Feedback" entry (footer) opening a sheet with 4 categories — suggest item, suggest recipe (uses `ItemSearch`), report broken (auto-captures `url` + optional recipe context), other.
- "Report this recipe" entry point on Combine's `DiscoveryToast` (`toasts.tsx:170`) passes recipe id + output + inputs into the sheet.
- `/admin/feedback` list page, status flip + dismiss + link out to `/admin/items/[id]`.

**Deferred (filing child tasks):**
- Inline 👍/👎 reactions on Combine recipes — separate data model (`recipe_reactions`), distinct UX surface. New task.
- Typed `track()` PostHog helper — CLAUDE.md asks for it but it doesn't exist yet; stub the call sites, file a task. New task.
- Admin email digest. New task.
- Open questions in body (auto-promote recipe suggestions to `draft` recipes; public credit) — leave to tyler's call during triage rollout. Noting in comment on landing.

**Decisions I'm making without asking:**
- Feedback status set: `open | triaged | dismissed | resolved` (not `in_progress`; admin can note resolution without full workflow).
- Recipe suggestions store free-text payload + referenced item ids; no auto-draft-recipe. Keeps schema simple; admin promotes manually from the triage row.
- Public credit: private only for now. Easy to add a `creditVisible` column later.
- Rate limit: reuse `limiters.reports` for all anonymous submits.

Starting implementation now.

**Landed — first slice.**

**Schema**
- `src/db/schema.ts` — new `feedback` table, `feedbackTypeEnum` (`suggest_item | suggest_recipe | report | other`), `feedbackStatusEnum` (`open | triaged | dismissed | resolved`), + exported types.
- `drizzle/0014_tearful_ultimo.sql` — generated migration. Run `npm run db:migrate` on next deploy.

**API**
- `src/app/api/feedback/route.ts` — public POST. Rate-limited via `limiters.reports` (10/hour per IP; signed-in users keyed by user id). Per-type payload shape validated; recipe suggestions require auth (401 if not). Max 4000 chars per text field, 1000 for url, 8 inputs max per recipe. Returns `{ ok, id }`.
- `src/app/api/admin/feedback/route.ts` — GET (list, newest first), admin-gated via `requireAdminApi`.
- `src/app/api/admin/feedback/[id]/route.ts` — PATCH (status + adminNote) and DELETE (hard-delete; `dismissed` covers soft).

**UI — user-facing**
- `src/components/common/FeedbackSheet.tsx` — 4-category sheet (portal via `ResponsiveSheet`). Seeded with `initial` prefill for in-context reports; auto-captures `window.location.href`. Non-signed-in users on `suggest_recipe` get a sign-in nudge instead of the form.
- `src/components/common/FeedbackLauncher.tsx` — footer button that opens the sheet.
- `src/components/common/Footer.tsx` — now async; reads session, passes `signedIn` into the launcher. All consumers are server components so no breakage.

**UI — Combine recipe report**
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/toasts.tsx` — `DiscoveryToast` gains an optional `onReport` prop; renders a small "Report this recipe" button inside the toast.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — wires `onReport` to open the FeedbackSheet pre-seeded with `type: "report"`, `category: "recipe_wrong"`, `recipeInputs` (names, with `=` separator before the output), and `itemId` (the recipe's output item id — the closest handle we have without plumbing recipe ids through the engine state).
- `src/components/combine/CombinePageBody.tsx` — reads session, passes `signedIn` to CombineBoard.

**Admin triage**
- `src/app/admin/feedback/page.tsx` + `FeedbackAdmin.tsx` — list, filter by status (defaults to `open`) and type, inline status flip, admin note, delete. Report rows link to `/admin/items/[id]` when an itemId is attached; recipe rows deep-link to `/admin/tree?recipe=...`.
- `src/app/admin/page.tsx` — "Feedback" link added to admin home actions.

**Styles**
- `src/app/globals.css` — `.cbdisc-report` (tiny outlined button, matches the toast's mono tagline treatment).

**Checks**
- `npm run typecheck` ✅
- `npm run lint` ✅ (only pre-existing warnings; my 3 lint errors fixed)
- `npm test` ✅ 296/296

**Deferred (child tasks filed):**
- T-0056 — Combine recipe 👍/👎 reactions
- T-0057 — typed PostHog `track()` helper (feedback route has a `// TODO track()` stub)
- T-0058 — admin feedback email digest

**Known caveats**
- The seed payload for "report this recipe" only carries `itemId` for the output, not the underlying `recipeId` — the engine state tracks the chosen inputs but not the DB recipe id. Easy to swap to `ItemSearch` later if admin noise gets high.
- No auto-promote of recipe suggestions to `draft` recipe rows — admin promotes manually from triage. Flagged in the body's open questions; leaving to tyler's call.

title: Public leaderboard for all modes (craft/link, combine, daily)
body:
Promote the existing private stats surface to public leaderboards. Scope is **all game modes**, not just craft/link.

Modes to cover:
- **Craft / link puzzle** — existing stats fields (par, moves, stars, hints, uniqueTargets, threeStarSolves).
- **Combine endless** — best score, total score, per-theme best (see `progress` with `kind='combine'`, `ref=<theme>`).
- **Combine daily** — per-day winners from `progress` rows where `result.daily=<day key>`.
- **Fast mode** — if it has its own leaderboard scope, include it; otherwise fold into endless.

**Already exploit-resistant (craft/link):**
- `won` is server-verified (`canMakeNow` + target match).
- Numeric fields clamped (moves ≥ par, time ≤ 24h, stars 0–3, hints ≤ 1000) so a hostile client can't skew aggregates.
- `par` recorded on each row is server-computed via `parFor`, not the client's claim.

**What's left to ship public:**
- Same stats functions work — swap the WHERE clause from "my user" to "top N over all users."
- Add eligibility gate: `handleLockedAt IS NOT NULL` (only players with a locked handle appear).
- Decide the public ranking metric per mode. Recommendation for craft: `uniqueTargets` or `threeStarSolves` (less exploitable than raw `totalSolves`). For combine: best score.
- Verify combine scores are also server-trusted end-of-run (check how `progress` rows are written).

Open:
- One `/leaderboard` with mode tabs, or per-mode routes?
- Caching / refresh cadence — materialized view, or live query with limit?
- Time-window tabs (all-time / monthly / weekly)?
- Privacy: confirm nothing beyond locked handle + metric is exposed.

title: Multi-lingual support: research approach
body:
How do we make Made Of multi-lingual?

Two separable layers to think about:

**1. UI chrome (buttons, labels, modals, how-to, copy)**
- Pick a framework: `next-intl`, `next-i18next`, or roll our own with App Router's built-in `generateStaticParams` on a `[locale]` segment.
- Translation workflow: hand-authored JSON, or AI-translated with human review?
- Fallback locale: English.

**2. Content (item names, descriptions, kinds, recipe notes, sources)**
- This is the hard part — content is in Postgres and admin-edited. Options:
  - Add `name_i18n jsonb` on `items` (and similar on kinds, recipes) with `{en: "...", es: "...", ...}`.
  - Separate `item_translations` table keyed by `(item_id, locale)`.
  - Machine-translate on write with an admin review queue (ties into T-0007 draft/review flow).
- Slug strategy: keep English slugs canonical, or per-locale slugs?
- SEO: hreflang tags, locale-specific sitemaps, llms.txt per locale?

**Other considerations:**
- Pictograms are visual — no translation needed.
- Dates, numbers, pluralization rules (use `Intl` APIs).
- Daily puzzle: does the "day key" shift by timezone/locale, or stay UTC-anchored?
- RTL support if we ever add Arabic/Hebrew.

Open:
- Which languages first? (Spanish, French, German, Japanese are typical starters.)
- Timing — before or after the public leaderboard / paid features land?
- Budget for translation (human vs machine)?

title: Items: consider adding Wikipedia links
body:
Idea: add a Wikipedia link on each item page so curious users can read more.

Unsure if good:

**For:**
- Low-effort way to deepen the "what is this?" experience.
- Fits the "sourced evidence for every link" ethos — Wikipedia as a tertiary "learn more" entry point.
- Could be auto-populated from the item slug/name for most items.

**Against:**
- Pulls users off-site at the moment they're engaged.

- Curation cost: wrong link on an ambiguous name (e.g., "Mercury" the element vs planet vs god) is worse than no link.

If pursued:
- Add `wikipedia_url` (nullable) to `items`, admin-editable in `/admin/tree` and `/admin/items/[id]`.
- Auto-suggest via Wikipedia API in admin, but require admin confirmation (no auto-link).
- Render as a small "Read on Wikipedia →" link in the item detail panel, visually de-emphasized vs internal sources.
- Mark as `rel="noopener"` external link; no prefetch.

Decision: park for now, revisit if users ask for "learn more" context.

title: Audit header auth-link hydration pattern (SSR stub → client hydrate)
body:
Possible auth issue to double-check:

Header no longer calls `getSession()` server-side. Instead the auth link renders a hidden stub during SSR and hydrates to "Sign in" or "Account" on the client.

Trade-offs noted:
- Tiny flash on first paint (invisible stub → real link). Deemed acceptable for a nav link.
- Static pages (`/terms`, `/privacy`, `/method`, 404) stay static — ISR benefit preserved.
- Dynamic pages behave the same as before.

Verify:
- No CLS from the stub → real-link swap (reserve width so layout doesn't shift).
- No accessibility regression: screen readers shouldn't announce the stub.
- Session cookie check still runs on protected routes server-side, not just client.
- Confirm the client-side session fetch is cached / dedup'd so every page view doesn't hit `/api/auth/session` fresh.
- PostHog identify still fires once the session is known (not during SSR).

If any of the above is off, decide between: (a) accept the flash and fix the specific regression, (b) move header back to a dynamic server component on routes that are already dynamic, or (c) use a cookie-presence hint during SSR to render the likely state and reconcile on hydrate.

title: Harden puzzle seeds / RNG against reverse engineering
body:
Make puzzle seeds + RNG hard to reverse so players can't predict tomorrow's daily, enumerate future targets, or farm the daily collection by brute-forcing the seed space.

**Current exposure (verify):**
- Daily seed may be derivable from the day key alone (e.g., `hash(dayKey)` or `mulberry32(dayKey)`) — anyone can recompute it locally.
- Combine daily puzzle and `/link` daily both use day-key seeding.
- Even though answers stay server-side (per CLAUDE.md hard rules), a predictable seed lets a client enumerate possible targets and precompute solutions.

**Options:**
1. **Server-side secret pepper.** Seed = `hash(dayKey || SECRET)`. Secret lives in env, never shipped to the client. Simple, effective; rotating the secret rolls all future puzzles.
2. **Stronger RNG.** Replace `mulberry32`/`splitmix` with a CSPRNG (`crypto.randomBytes` seeded once per day by the server, result stored in a `daily_puzzle` row). Clients never see the seed, only the resulting puzzle payload.
3. **Store generated puzzles, not seeds.** A scheduled job generates each day's puzzle ahead of time and writes it to Postgres. Clients get the puzzle spec, never the generation function.

**Recommendation:** combine 1 + 3 — nightly job generates and stores puzzles using a peppered seed; clients only ever see the materialized puzzle.

Open:
- Audit where the seed is currently derived — likely in `src/combine/...` and `src/link/...`.
- If puzzles are generated on-demand, add the pepper now; add the stored-puzzle job later.

- Handle for timezone — daily key should still be UTC-anchored (see T-0014 open question).

title: Lighthouse: hit 100 across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO
body:
Target: 100/100 on all four Lighthouse categories (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO) for the key routes.

**Routes to score:**
- `/` (landing)
- `/link` (daily link puzzle)
- `/combine` (Combine mode)
- `/craft` (From scratch)
- `/i/[slug]` and `/explore/[slug]` (bowtie / item page — sample a few popular items)
- `/about`, `/method`

**Approach:**
- Run Lighthouse (mobile preset) on each route, capture current scores.
- File sub-issues per category hit, since fixes diverge: perf = bundle/images/LCP, a11y = labels/contrast/landmarks, best-practices = HTTPS/console errors/deprecated APIs, SEO = meta/hreflang/structured data.
- Automate: add a Lighthouse CI step so regressions surface on PRs.

Related: T-0021 (fast page load — perf category contributes directly).

Open:
- Which routes are must-hit-100 vs best-effort?
- Acceptable to score mobile only, or desktop too?
- Does running behind Cloudflare skew results — test against prod, not local.

title: Extremely fast page load across all routes
body:
Goal: extremely fast page loads everywhere — the app should feel instant.

**Targets (mobile, p75):**
- LCP < 1.5s
- INP < 100ms
- CLS < 0.05
- First byte < 200ms from edge

**Levers to pull:**
- **Edge caching.** Cloudflare caches static + ISR-friendly routes aggressively. Confirm cache-control headers per route.
- **Static where possible.** `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/method`, 404, about — keep static (see T-0018 auth audit; header must not force dynamic rendering).
- **Item pages via ISR.** `/i/[slug]` revalidate-on-demand when admin edits, otherwise static.
- **Bundle budget.** Audit `npm run build` output; split heavy routes (Combine board, admin) so landing doesn't pay for them.
- **Font strategy.** Chivo + Chivo Mono: self-host, `font-display: swap`, preload only the weights used above the fold.
- **Image strategy.** Pictograms are inline SVG (good). OG images via `next/og` generated on the fly with cache.
- **Preload critical API calls.** First Combine board fetch, first item neighbourhood — can be inlined into the initial RSC payload.
- **Client JS trim.** Audit "use client" boundaries — keep them tight.

Related: T-0020 (Lighthouse 100 — overlaps on perf category).

Open:
- Set a real-user metrics (RUM) target, not just lab Lighthouse — PostHog web vitals plugin or Vercel-style web-vitals endpoint.
- Budgets in CI: fail PR if bundle grows > N kB.

title: Location-aware cookies: regional defaults (timezone, locale, daily key)
body:
Idea: use location signals to set sensible defaults via cookies — e.g. locale, timezone, daily puzzle rollover, measurement units.

**Sources:**
- Cloudflare already provides `CF-IPCountry` (and more if enabled). Trust Cloudflare per CLAUDE.md ("Trust only Cloudflare").
- `Accept-Language` for language guess.
- Client-side `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` for timezone (cookie after first visit).

**Candidate uses:**
- Default locale once multi-lingual ships (T-0014).
- "Your day" rollover for daily puzzle: show local-time rollover countdown even though the day key stays UTC-anchored (see T-0019 open question).
- Units / date formatting.
- A/B default theme (if ever).

**Design:**
- Set a single short cookie (`made_of_region` or similar) on first request from Cloudflare headers.
- Keep it server-readable so SSR can render with the right defaults — avoids a hydration flip.
- Non-essential cookie → cookie banner implications (consent, GDPR). Verify current cookie policy covers this.

**Hard rules to respect:**
- Don't send child-profile-style data to analytics.
- Daily puzzle *content* must stay UTC-anchored and identical globally (fairness for leaderboards) — this cookie only affects display/UX, not which puzzle you get.

Open:
- Is a cookie needed at all vs reading CF headers on every request? Cookie is useful for client-side components + reducing header reliance.
- Consent flow: this is probably "functional" not "analytics" — document it accordingly.

title: Combine: hide top nav bar while playing
body:
Users currently have to drag/scroll the page down to bring game parts into view because the top nav bar is eating viewport.

Options:
- Hide the nav entirely on `/combine` while a run is active; show on pause/game-over.
- Auto-hide on scroll (slide up when user scrolls down, back on scroll up).
- Make nav sticky but much shorter on the Combine route.

Preference: hide-while-playing is cleanest; a small "back to menu" affordance can live inside the game UI itself.

Open:
- Same treatment for `/craft` and `/link`, or Combine only?
- Keep an escape hatch (tap anywhere non-tile reveals nav briefly)?

title: Offline gameplay (PWA / service worker)
body:
Can players continue playing (Combine endless at least) with no network?

Shape:
- PWA + service worker caching the app shell and a snapshot of theme items.
- Offline-only modes: Combine endless and Craft could work if the item graph + recipes are cached.
- Offline-blocked: daily puzzles (seeds come from server per T-0019), leaderboards, discoveries sync (queue + reconcile on reconnect).

Hard-rule constraints:
- "Never send the whole graph to the browser" — caching a theme's item set is OK (it's one scoped payload); caching the whole graph is not.
- Server still owns all verification; offline runs that affect score/collection need a resync validation step on reconnect, otherwise accept them as "offline only" and don't count toward leaderboards.

Open:
- Scope v1 to "install prompt + offline shell + cached assets" before syncing play state.
- iOS PWA quirks around service worker lifetime, background sync.

title: Decide: music / sound effects on by default?
body:
Question: should music and SFX be on by default?

Arguments for on:
- Juicier first impression; game feels alive.
- Most casual puzzle games (Block Blast etc.) default on.

Arguments for off:
- Browser autoplay policies may still block music until user gesture — SFX usually fine on first interaction.
- Workplace/public browsing: surprise audio is a known friction / closed tab trigger.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` adjacent sensibility.

Recommendation:
- **SFX on by default**, triggered by first user gesture (safe under autoplay rules).
- **Music off by default**, opt-in via settings toggle (persisted in a small local-storage key + optional user pref in DB).
- Visible mute button in-game.

Open:
- Audio assets ready? If not, this is blocked on content.

comments.body: Resolved as part of T-0055: music and SFX now default on (`src/combine/storage.ts:48` → `{ music: "piano", sfx: true, vol: 80 }`, matching useState initial at `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:281`). Autoplay rules still handled by the first-pointerdown unlock. Existing users' saved prefs are preserved.

title: Play-testing plan
body:
Define a repeatable play-testing plan so feedback is structured, not anecdotal.

Shape:
- **Who:** target personas (kids 8–12, casual puzzle players, curious adults, educators?). Need a short recruiting script.
- **What:** session structure — intro (2m), free play (10–15m), structured tasks ("try to finish the daily link," "get a 3-age combine run"), semi-structured interview (10m).
- **Where:** in-person first round (lowest friction for watching), remote sessions over screen-share after.
- **What to capture:**
  - Where does the player get stuck? (First combine, understanding bands, finding the daily, reading a bowtie.)
  - What do they say they *think* each mode is before playing?
  - Discovery moments — did any badge/age-up land as intended?
  - Rage-quit triggers.
- **Note-taking template:** one page per session, timestamped observations + direct quotes.
- **Follow-up loop:** every 2 weeks, batch findings into a changelog/PR triage pass.

Open:
- Budget for recruiting incentives?
- Record sessions? (Consent + storage policy needed.)
- Separate plan for Combine (score/collection game) vs Link (daily puzzle)?

title: Audit Combine game-state persistence: DB vs localStorage, tamper + refresh
body:
Questions to answer together — they're all the same audit:

1. **Is in-progress game state saved in the DB, or only localStorage?**
2. **Can users manipulate or reset local storage to cheat (inflate score, reroll bands, undo losses)?**
3. **Does refreshing the page reset scores / lose the current run?**

Expected behaviour (to confirm matches implementation):
- **Finished runs** write to `progress` (server-side, authoritative) — cannot be tampered.
- **In-progress run** likely lives in client state + localStorage for resume-on-refresh. That's fine *if* it never affects the final `progress` write without server validation.
- A client that edits localStorage can give themselves a higher "current score," but if the server replays or verifies the end-of-run write, the leaderboard stays clean.

Action:
- Map every piece of Combine state and where it's stored (client only, localStorage, DB).
- Verify end-of-run write is server-trusted (score computed server-side, not accepted from client). If not, fix before public leaderboards (T-0012).
- Decide: should in-progress runs *also* persist server-side so a mid-run device switch works? (Nice-to-have; not security-critical.)
- Confirm refresh behaviour matches intent — losing a run on refresh is bad UX; preserving it from localStorage is fine as long as it can't be gamed.

Related:
- T-0012 (public leaderboard — depends on this audit landing clean).
- T-0019 (puzzle seed hardening — adjacent concern).

comments.body:
**Approach**

Reading only — this audit is a map + risk assessment, not a code change. If anything needs fixing I'll file follow-up tasks rather than inflate this one.

Files to map:
- `src/combine/storage.ts` — localStorage layer (save/load/hydrate + side tables)
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — resume-on-mount, auto-save effect, end-of-run write
- `src/app/api/combine/result/route.ts` — the DB-authoritative write
- `src/app/api/combine/collection/route.ts` — discoveries endpoint

Three questions I'll answer:
1. Where does every piece of in-progress state live? (expect: localStorage only, by design)
2. Can a client inflate `score`, `made`, `age`, `season` on the final write? (expect: yes, with clamps)
3. Does refresh actually resume? (expect: yes for classic endless + daily; no for fast by design)

I'll call out anything unexpected and leave the "add server-side in-progress persistence" nice-to-have for a separate ticket if warranted.

**Audit complete — findings**

**Q1 — State map**

In-progress state is localStorage-only. Keys in `src/combine/storage.ts:31-39`:
- `madeof:cbsave`, `madeof:cbsave:daily` — full StoredGame projection (board, tray, score, RNG seed, hold, crumb, shelf, found-this-run, etc.)
- `madeof:cbbest:<theme>[:fast]` — best scores
- `madeof:cbdaily` — today's DailyResult
- `madeof:cbfound` — device-local lifetime collection (signed-out fallback)
- `madeof:cbseenages:<theme>`, `madeof:cbonboarded`, sound keys — UI/side tables

DB authoritative only for finished runs (`progress` via `src/app/api/combine/result/route.ts:78-86`) and discoveries for signed-in users (`combine_discoveries` via `/api/combine/collection`).

**Q2 — Tamper surface**

Yes, cheatable. Mitigated only by clamps, not verification.
- `result/route.ts:15-17` explicitly says "we trust the client's totals." Clamps: score ≤ 1M, made ≤ 100k, age ≤ 100, season ≤ serverSeason. Below those ceilings a tampered client posts anything.
- localStorage edits propagate to the `progress` write because the server never replays events.
- `/api/combine/collection` POST accepts any existing item id as a discovery — full-collection unlock is a one-shot POST.
- Daily puzzles: `dailySeed(day)` is derived client-side; the result route accepts any `daily` key in the right format with no replay check.
- Clearing localStorage just starts a fresh game (RNG seed is in the save, so re-rolls are free; no "undo a loss" vector).

**Q3 — Refresh behaviour**

Works as designed. No bug.
- Auto-save `CombineBoard.tsx:790-794` writes after every settled transition (skips while `state.choosing` is open).
- Mount resume `CombineBoard.tsx:167-217` loads daily-done + endless save, hydrates if present. `?d=<day>` deep-links today's daily.
- Intentional exceptions in `saveGame` (`storage.ts:152-155`): debug runs and Fast mode never persist (Fast is score-only by design).
- `loadGame` drops a save on: version mismatch (`SAVE_VERSION=6`, bumped at v5→v6 for the band layout change), size mismatch, stale daily, theme mismatch, unknown item ids (content drift), age ≥ bundle length.

**Why users would report lost runs**

Not a code bug. Likely:
1. They were in Fast mode (no save by design).
2. A `SAVE_VERSION` or `DAILY_EPOCH` bump between visits silently dropped the save.
3. Content edits in admin removed/renamed an item in their board → `loadGame` drop at `storage.ts:224-228`.
4. Content shrank the bundle's age list → drop at `storage.ts:233`.
5. localStorage unavailable (private mode, Safari ITP eviction, quota, cross-device expectations).

**Follow-ups to file**

- **T-NEW (P1, blocks T-0012):** Make Combine leaderboard-safe before public leaderboards ship. Options: server-side move replay against a signed RNG seed, or a signed/HMAC'd run token that the client posts back. Today the route trusts clamped client totals.
- **T-NEW (P2):** Harden `/api/combine/collection` POST — only accept discoveries that are reachable in the current theme's recipe graph from base ingredients, not any item id in the DB.
- **T-NEW (P3, nice-to-have):** Server-side in-progress snapshot keyed by user+theme for cross-device / cache-clear resilience. Not security-critical since the leaderboard is where cheating matters.
- **T-NEW (P3):** Telemetry on `loadGame` drops (reason: version / size / content / age) so silent resets from content drift become visible instead of appearing as "lost my game."

Marking done + needs_review. Not filing the follow-ups automatically — want your call on scope/priorities before I create them.

title: Combine Fast mode: 3-step combines not 2, surface history, confirm no collection
body:
Three Fast-mode items bundled — all small, all connected:

**1. Difficulty: 3-step combines, not 2.**
- Fast currently restricts to **2-ingredient recipes** (pair-only). These are too easy — the player just has to match two tiles.
- Change Fast's recipe filter so combines require **3 steps** (3 ingredients). Harder to line up on the board, longer chains before the output lands.
- Where: `src/combine/data.ts:361` — `recipes = recipes.filter((r) => r.all.length === 2);`
- NOTE: nothing to do with audio, time, or wall-clock timers. This is purely about `recipe.all.length` — the number of ingredients you have to assemble.

Open:
- Should Fast allow BOTH 2 and 3 (`length <= 3`), or STRICTLY 3 (`length === 3`)? Strict 3 is cleaner conceptually; `<= 3` is more forgiving and keeps the dense combo feel. Confirm with user.
- Rename? "Fast · 3-step" vs leaving it "Fast." Probably leave the name alone — the mode is still score-chase.
- Everyday Fast: smaller KB, may not have enough 3-ingredient recipes to be playable. Check both themes' pair-count after the filter change before shipping.
- Rebalance Fast's `ageNeed` / termination — longer per-combine means fewer combines per run; may need to lower the stop threshold.

**2. Why no history showing for Fast mode?**
- Finished runs don't appear in history / stats panel. Bug?
- Verify `progress` rows are being written for Fast with the right `kind`/`ref`.
- Verify the history view's query includes Fast runs (might be filtering only `combine` without the `ref=fast` sub-case, or vice versa).

**3. Is there a collection? Seems like it?**
- Per the memory ([Combine fast mode design](project_combine_fast_mode.md)): "Fast is score-only, no collection unlocks."
- User is observing something that looks like a collection — investigate whether Fast is accidentally writing to `combine_discoveries` (endless scope).
- If yes: stop writing. If no but UI implies a collection exists: fix the copy/UI in Fast.

title: Combine helper: "move" should use drag + highlight/tick/cross interaction
body:
The "move" helper's current interaction doesn't match how combines feel. Make it consistent with the main combine gesture:

- **Drag** the selected tile to a destination.
- Show **highlight** on hover/drop target.
- Show **tick** on a valid drop, **cross** on an invalid one.
- Snap back if invalid.

Why: parity with the main board interaction is lower cognitive load, and the helper will be more discoverable.

Where: likely `src/combine/.../helpers/move.tsx` (confirm).

Open:
- Does this change the helper's cost / count-per-run? (See T-0004 / T-0010 for tunables.)

title: Combine: investigate "unique ages" scoring — appears not to be unique
body:
Observation: the "unique ages" scoring/contribution appears to be counting duplicates instead of unique entries. It's meant to be unique but isn't behaving that way.

Action:
- Find where "unique ages" is computed — likely in Combine score/age tracking (`src/combine/.../score.ts` or similar).
- Check whether it's using `new Set(...)` / dedupe before counting, vs just counting all age-ups.
- Verify against a repro run: age up to the same tier twice in a row — does the "unique ages" counter go up by 1 or 2?
- Fix the dedupe + add a unit test so it doesn't regress.

Open:
- Is the bug in the computation, the display, or both? (Maybe the data is unique but the UI is reading the wrong field.)
- Does this affect any existing `progress` rows / leaderboard numbers that need backfilling?

T-0051 shipped in commit `23ea3ef`: `state.ageMade++` now gates on `!state.found.includes(recipe.out)`, with a test fixture in `src/combine/__tests__/engine.test.ts` covering "same item twice → ageMade goes up by 1".
- The end-of-run `GameOverCard` only shows `age reached` (single highest age), not a "unique ages" count. The Ages sheet shows `X/Y` for the current age and `Done (X/Y)` for past ages after T-0054.

Given T-0051 is the only duplicates-vs-unique age counter bug in the codebase, and T-0030 was filed before T-0051 landed, treating T-0030 as the earlier, less-precise report of the same bug.

If there was something *else* you meant by "unique ages scoring" (e.g. an admin dashboard field or a leaderboard column I missed), ping back with a screenshot or the exact surface and I'll reopen.

title: Hint should be dismissed by user, not auto-timed
body:
Hints currently time out on their own. Change to: hint stays visible until the user dismisses it (tap/click the hint, close button, or completes the suggested combine).

Why: auto-timed hints are frustrating when a player is reading/thinking — they vanish mid-decision.

Scope — likely Combine's hint helper (assumption, confirm):
- Find the hint component and remove the timer.
- Add an explicit dismiss affordance (× button, tap to dismiss, or auto-dismiss only when the hinted action is performed).

Open:
- Does this apply to other surfaces too (Craft hints, Link puzzle hints)? If yes, bundle the fix.
- Should the hint stay pinned across turns, or dismiss itself when the board state changes enough that it's no longer accurate?

comments.body:
**Already implemented — closing as done.**

Audit of the current hint flow:

- **`src/components/combine/board-parts/toasts.tsx:74-135`** — `HintToast` is a plain `<div role="status" onClick={onDismiss}>`. The whole toast is a tap-to-dismiss target, and the inline copy reads "Hint · tap to close" (line 109) plus a trailing "Tap to close." (line 99, except the `teach` variant which has its own closing line).
- **`src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:237`** — `hintToast` state is a plain `useState<HintResult | null>`. No `useEffect` with a timer paired to `setHintToast(null)`. Searched all `setTimeout`/`setInterval` in the file; none touch hint state.
- **`CombineBoard.tsx:1063-1066`** — ESC key also dismisses the hint (part of the overlay-dismiss chain).

The task's other open questions:
- **Hint stays pinned across board-state changes.** It does — nothing invalidates it except user dismiss or ESC. If the player's next placement makes the hinted combo stale, the toast still shows the old recipe. Not changing this: the copy phrases hints as suggestions ("Try this:"), and auto-dismissing on board changes would be a different pattern than what users expect from "tap to close."
- **Other surfaces (Craft, Link).** Out of scope — this task scopes to the Combine hint helper and the Combine hint is the only one described as auto-timed.

No code changes.

title: Audio: pause on tab/visibility change, resume on return
body:
Audio keeps playing when the user switches tabs / minimizes the window. It should pause when the tab is hidden and resume when it becomes visible again.

Shape:
- Listen for `document.visibilitychange`.
- `document.hidden === true` → pause all audio (music + SFX queue).
- `document.hidden === false` → resume music if it was playing before; don't auto-replay queued SFX.
- Also respect the user's mute preference — don't resume if they muted while away.

Edge cases:
- Mobile browsers suspend JS when tab is backgrounded, so audio may already stop on iOS/Android — test on both.
- Don't restart music from the beginning on return; seek-resume where it left off.
- If the player returns to a game-over screen, don't resume gameplay music.

Related: T-0025 (audio defaults).

Open:
- Should music fade out over 200–300ms instead of hard-pause? Probably yes for music, no for SFX.

title: Admin: mobile-friendly recipe editor (e.g., add Na + Cl → salt on phone)
body:
Example that exposed the problem: admin tries to add `Na + Cl → salt` while on mobile and the recipe editor is painful to use.

Pain points to confirm + fix:
- Item picker likely assumes desktop (wide dropdown, tiny hit targets, hover states).
- Multi-input recipes (two items feeding one output) require several picker interactions — each needs to be thumb-friendly.
- The link-type selector (`f`, `w`, `n`, `s`, `e`) + confidence (`established`/`strong`/`debated`/`hypothesis`) menus are probably too small on mobile.
- Keyboard pops over the picker on iOS, pushing content around.

Where: `/admin/tree` inline editor, `/admin/items/[id]`.

Shape of fix:
- Bottom-sheet item picker on mobile instead of a dropdown — full-width search, recent/popular items at top.
- Large tap targets for link-type + confidence (segmented control, not a `<select>`).
- One-tap "add input" that opens the picker, not a two-step reveal.
- Preserve scroll position after save so you don't lose your place in the tree.

Open:
- Is admin-on-mobile a supported path, or do we expect admin from desktop only? If desktop-only, we still want *some* mobile usability for quick fixes in the field, but we don't need parity.
- Could this flow be driven from the user feedback report (T-0011) — admin taps a report, lands directly on the right recipe editor with inputs prefilled?

comments.body:
Content note on the Na+Cl → salt example:

Salt in the graph is really **two distinct items**: *natural salt* (sea/rock salt — geologic / biological source) and *chemical salt* (NaCl synthesised from elements). We currently only have **natural salt**.

Implications:
- When this example is used to test the mobile recipe editor, we actually need to **add chemical salt** as a separate item first, then wire `Na + Cl → chemical salt` to it (not to natural salt).
- Natural salt keeps its existing `s` (comes-from) link to seawater / rock, etc.
- Avoid conflating them in a single item — the provenance (big-bang → ... → salt) is different for each.

This is a content task that should probably live on its own, but worth flagging here since it's the test case for the editor UX.

title: Combine: distinguish new-to-collection vs age discovery; notify on collection unlock
body:
Two things conflated in the current UI, and one is silent:

1. **Age discovery** — first time you make an item within the *current run* (contributes to age-up progress).
2. **Collection discovery** — first time you *ever* make an item in the endless lifetime scope (adds to `combine_discoveries` with `scope='endless'`).

Problems:
- Visually they look nearly identical — players can't tell "I unlocked this for my lifetime collection" vs "I made this in this run."
- A **new collection** unlock may not be surfacing to the user at all (no toast / banner / sparkle), so the milestone feels invisible.

Fixes:
- Different treatments:
  - Age discovery: subtle highlight on the tile + age-up progress bar tick.
  - Collection discovery (first-ever): louder — toast with "New in your collection: <item>", pictogram animation, optional sound.
- On the item tile itself, a small "★ new" badge the first time it enters the collection, cleared next session.
- Make sure the notification also fires for daily-scope collection unlocks — but worded differently so players don't confuse scopes.

Related:
- Partial completion milestones (T-0008) — collection notifications are the atomic unit under those.
- Audio defaults (T-0025) — unlock jingle lives here.

Open:
- Should the game briefly pause on a collection unlock to make the moment land, or stay fully live?
- Account/stats page should also show "last collection unlock" to anchor the long-tail progression.

comments.body:
Approach:

**Problem definition:**
- `state.found` tracks first-make-this-run (age discovery). Already visible via `fx.discover` cell sparkle + the existing `DiscoveryToast`.
- `useCollection.found` tracks lifetime unlocks (via `/api/combine/collection`). Currently added silently on `discovery` events — **no distinct UI**.
- Players can't tell "new to my lifetime collection" from "just made it again this run", which is the bigger of the two moments.

**Distinction keys:**
- **Age discovery (silent/subtle):** every first-make-this-run — `fx.discover`, age-progress bar tick, pictogram sparkle. KEEP as-is.
- **Collection unlock (loud):** first-ever lifetime find. Needs its own toast grammar, different wording for `endless` vs `daily`, optional SFX, non-blocking.

**Scope decisions (narrowing the task body):**
1. **No game pause** on collection unlock. Non-blocking toast with fade (~3s) so gameplay stays live. The chain animation finishes before the toast appears (sequence after `fx.discover` clears).
2. **Queue multiple unlocks.** Chain reactions can first-discover several lifetime items in one move (star-chain promote especially). Toast queue with 450ms stagger so they don't stack visually.
3. **Daily scope wording:** "Daily puzzle discovery — won't affect your endless collection." Keeps scopes mentally separate (fits T-0068 memory note).
4. **Signed-out / fast mode:** no toast. Signed-out players have no lifetime collection; fast mode is score-only by design.
5. **"★ new" per-tile badge:** persist via a new localStorage set (`cbNewUnlocks`) that clears when the player opens the item's DetailCard. Survives reload. Rendered on the Shelf tiles (already the discovery surface).
6. **Account/stats:** out of scope for v1 — flag as a follow-up. The in-game toast is the delightful part; the stats surface is a nice-to-have anchor.
7. **SFX:** piggyback on existing sfx-on flag via `playFx("discover")` or similar. If no dedicated unlock sound exists yet, reuse the existing discovery sound at higher gain, or skip the audio piece in v1 and file a follow-up for a bespoke sound.

**Implementation plan:**
1. **CombineBoard.tsx:** new state `collectionToasts: Array<{item, scope}>` + queue management. After `useCollection.add(ids)` succeeds for a run, diff against prior `collection.keys()` to find NEW unlocks, enqueue toasts for each. Daily/endless scope passed through.
2. **New component** `CollectionToast.tsx` — similar to `DiscoveryToast` but visually distinct (crown/sparkle icon instead of tier color, "New in your collection!" header, scope-dependent subtext). Auto-dismisses after 3s or on tap.
3. **Shelf.tsx / CombineTile.tsx:** ★ badge on items where `tileId ∈ newUnlocksSet`. Clears when DetailCard opens for that item.
4. **Storage:** new `loadNewUnlocks()` / `saveNewUnlocks()` keyed `madeof:cbnew:<scope>` → `string[]` of item ids.
5. **CSS:** new `.cbnew-toast` class, optional `cbspark` reuse for the pictogram, accent color scheme for ★ badge on tile.
6. **Audio:** check `src/combine/audio/sfx.ts` for existing sounds. Use the loudest one available for unlock; otherwise skip and file follow-up.

**Not changing:**
- Age discovery visuals (`fx.discover`, `DiscoveryToast`) stay exactly as they are.
- `useCollection` API stays unchanged — just diff its returned map.

**Tests:**
- Engine already emits `discovery` events on first-finds; the new UI logic is React side (hard to unit-test without RTL). Will add a lightweight unit test in `useCollection` or wherever the diff logic ends up to confirm "new unlocks" is computed correctly given before/after sets.

**Open after landing (file as follow-ups if you agree):**
- Account/stats "last unlock" surface.
- Dedicated unlock SFX if the current library doesn't have one that reads as "milestone."
- Interaction with T-0008 milestones — same event stream.

Landed.

**Files changed:**
- `src/combine/audio/sfx.ts` — new `"unlock"` SfxKind. Six-note climbing arpeggio with higher velocity and longer tail than `"discover"`, so lifetime unlocks sound distinctly rarer than age finds.
- `src/combine/storage.ts` — `loadNewUnlocks` / `saveNewUnlocks` / `addNewUnlocks` / `clearNewUnlock`, keyed `madeof:cbnew:<scope>`. Set-shaped; add returns the newly-added ids so callers can gate side effects.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx`:
  - Discovery toast gated on `firstLifetime` (age-only discoveries no longer trigger the modal — they still show the per-cell sparkle via `fx.discover` and bump the shelf).
  - `"unlock"` SFX for lifetime finds; `"discover"` keeps playing for age-only.
  - New `newUnlocks: Set<string>` state hydrated from localStorage per scope; `newUnlocksScopeRef` to detect scope flips.
  - `addNewUnlocks` called on `firstLifetime` discoveries (skipped in fast mode).
  - DetailCard open clears the badge via `clearNewUnlock` + state update.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/Shelf.tsx` — new `newUnlocks?: ReadonlySet<string>` prop; renders a ★ badge + accent outline on tiles in the set. `aria-label` announces "new in your collection".
- `src/app/globals.css` — `.cbslot.unlock` accent outline + `.cbunlock-star` badge (top-left, opposite the bottom-right count).

**Not changed (per plan):**
- Age-discovery visuals (`fx.discover` sparkle, age-progress tick) are untouched.
- `useCollection` API unchanged — the `firstLifetime` flag was already being computed at line 651; we just gate UI on it correctly now.
- No pause on unlock; non-blocking toast with existing fade.

**Follow-up candidates (file when you want):**
- Dedicated unlock-sfx tuning — current implementation is louder/longer/higher-pitched than discover but no bespoke timbre.
- Account/stats "last unlock" surface (deferred from task body).
- Milestone events (T-0008) can subscribe to the same "firstLifetime" signal; wire when T-0008 is picked up.
- Daily-scope wording tweak: currently the toast copy is identical for endless and daily. Consider "Daily puzzle discovery — won't affect your endless collection" footer line for daily.

**Tests:** `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 315/315 (no new tests — all changes are UI-side; existing engine semantics unchanged).

**Known gap:** no RTL/E2E coverage for the toast/sfx/badge wiring (consistent with the rest of the codebase; no component tests for CombineBoard).

title: Admin analytics: usage counts on items, recipes, and Combine surfaces
body:
Surface "how many times has this been seen / made / used" on admin pages so curation decisions have data behind them.

**Items (admin tree + per-item page):**
- Views on `/i/[slug]` (from PostHog or server logs).
- Times included as a target in a daily/link puzzle.
- Times created as an output in Combine runs.
- Times appearing in anyone's endless collection (unique users).

**Recipes:**
- Times executed in Combine runs.
- Times viewed in bowtie / explore.
- Last-used timestamp — stale recipes surface for review.

**Combine surfaces:**
- Per-theme: sessions, median run length, distribution of ages reached.
- Per-tile pair: how often attempted, success rate (did it produce a valid output or dead-end).
- Daily puzzle: completion rate, median moves, 3-star rate.
- Fast mode: attempts, timeout-loss rate (feeds back into T-0028 timer tuning).

Source:
- PostHog events (already tracked via the `track()` helper) for view/attempt counts.
- Postgres `progress` + `combine_discoveries` for authoritative run/collection data.
- Consider a nightly materialized rollup to avoid heavy queries in admin.

Where it shows:
- `/admin/tree` — a "usage" column (collapsible, mobile-safe).
- `/admin/items/[id]` — a usage panel.
- `/admin/combine/themes` — theme-level dashboard.
- Maybe a new `/admin/analytics` landing page that pulls it together.

Open:
- Window: all-time, last 30d, or both?
- Do we need per-tile-pair stats stored permanently, or can PostHog answer this on demand?
- Privacy: aggregate counts only — never show which user did what.

title: Admin: configure age progression per Combine mode
body:
Give admins an editor to configure age progression for each Combine mode (endless, daily, fast, future themes).

Config surface:
- Ordered list of ages (e.g., Primordial → Elemental → Molecular → …), with name, threshold rules, visuals/tier color mapping.
- Per-mode overrides (Fast may have a shorter chain; a theme like "Everyday" may use a different progression entirely).
- Preview: show how the current rules play out against a sample run.

Backing:
- Depends on T-0005 (move age chains out of client `types.ts` into server-sourced data).
- Lives alongside T-0010 (admin game controls) — this is one surface within that broader settings area.

Validation:
- Each age must have at least one reachable item in the mode's theme (reuse the reachability validator from `/admin/combine/themes`).
- Thresholds must be monotonically increasing.
- Changes versioned so in-progress runs don't break mid-session — either freeze a run's age chain at start, or hot-swap with a warning.

Open:
- Should ages be first-class DB entities (`combine_ages` table) or JSON on the mode/theme config?
- Does changing the age chain retroactively affect historical `progress`/leaderboard rows? Probably no — freeze run-time snapshots.

title: High-scores page: daily combine + extensible home for all games, public + personal
body:
A dedicated high-scores page as a player-facing destination — distinct from the backend leaderboard work in T-0012.

**Shape:**
- `/scores` (or similar) as the single home for high scores across every game Made Of ships.
- Tabs or sections: Combine endless, Combine daily, Combine fast, Craft/link puzzle, and room for future modes.
- **Daily combine** gets a per-day board — today's winners pinned, scrollable history by date.
- **Two views per board:**
  - **Public** — top N across all users (eligibility: handle locked, per T-0012).
  - **Personal** — your rank + your best, surfaced even if you're not in the top N. Shows your personal bests over time.
- Social share: deep-link to a specific day's daily board.

**Depends on:**
- T-0012 (leaderboard backend — the stats functions, eligibility, metric decisions).
- T-0010 / T-0036 (admin controls — to toggle visibility / eligibility rules).

**Hard rules to respect:**
- Handles only (locked), no email/name exposure.
- Combine run scores must be server-trusted (see T-0027 state audit).
- Daily seeds must be unpredictable (T-0019) so the daily board is fair.

Open:
- One tabbed page vs separate routes per game? Tabbed is simpler now; separate routes scale better for SEO later.
- How far back does the daily history go (all-time, last 30 days)?
- Does the page require auth, or is it public with a prompt to sign in for personal view?

title: Combine: Hardcore mode (no info, no helpers, faster crumble)
body:
New Combine variant: **Hardcore mode.** Strips away all assists so scoring is pure.

Rules:
- **No tile info.** Don't show item name/kind on hover or tap — pictogram only. Player identifies tiles by memory.
- **No helpers** (reroll, move, hint, etc.).
- **No recipe helpers** — no "possible combines" preview, no auto-suggestions.
- **No on-hover helpers** — no tooltips, no highlight-compatible, no "this pair works" glow.
- **Double crumble time** — tiles crumble/expire 2× faster than endless, raising time pressure.

Shape:
- Same scoring system as endless (feeds leaderboards), but **separate leaderboard scope** so hardcore scores don't mix with assisted-endless.
- Shares endless collection scope? → **decide** (recommendation: yes, successful combines still unlock collection since the game is objectively harder, not a parallel universe).
- Fast mode interaction: hardcore + fast would be near-unplayable — gate behind an explicit "yes I know what I'm doing" selector or keep them mutually exclusive.

Admin tunables (via T-0010 / T-0036):
- Which assist flags are "hardcore off" — keep it config-driven so the ruleset can evolve.
- Crumble multiplier (default 2×).

Open:
- UI entry: in the Combine landing, as a third mode button next to Endless/Fast? Or an "intensity" toggle on Endless?
- Prestige treatment: a distinct tile color / border for hardcore runs on the high-scores page (T-0037)?
- Does this interact with T-0001 (link-mode options / recipe complexity picker)? Hardcore is the opposite axis — most-complex, fewest-assists.

title: Monetisation: define free vs paid tier (recipes, modes, pricing model)
body:
Define the monetisation model for Made Of. Starting considerations from user:

- **Free to play, limited recipes.** Core modes playable, but the recipe graph is capped — e.g., first N recipes per item, or a subset of themes, or a tier cap (F/N/M free; C/P/S paid).
- **One-off payment** unlocks all recipes. No subscription, no ads.
- **Hardcore mode** (T-0038) gated behind the paid tier.

**Open design questions:**

- *What counts as "limited"?* Options:
  - Cap unique Combine discoveries at N per lifetime (then "unlock full collection").
  - Hide late-game tier items (C/P/S) until paid.
  - Theme gating — "Everything" free, "Everyday" + future themes paid.
  - Daily puzzles free, endless capped at low scores without paid.
- *What's paid gets:*
  - Full recipe graph / full collection.
  - Hardcore mode (T-0038).
  - Maybe: `/api/items/:id/everything` (already noted as paid-only in CLAUDE.md).
  - Maybe: priority on leaderboard eligibility or cosmetic distinction.
- *What stays free forever* (table stakes for a playable first impression):
  - Daily link puzzle.
  - At least one Combine theme at endless scope.
  - Item pages and bowtie explore.

**Pricing anchors:**
- One-off: $5 / $10 / $15 / $20 — small enough to be an impulse, large enough to feel one-time.
- Family/gift option (one payment unlocks for a shared account or multiple handles).

**Infrastructure notes:**
- Stripe is already in the planned stack (CLAUDE.md).
- Entitlement checks must be server-side (hard rule).
- Need an `entitlements` table keyed by user id, with status + source + purchased_at.
- UI can hint what's gated, but never ship gated data to the client.

**Risks / things to decide:**
- Is this child-friendly? Kids 8–12 are a plausible audience; one-off payment avoids subscription traps but may need adult-controlled purchase flow.
- Refund policy (digital one-off is usually no-refund, but be humane for mispurchases).
- Regional pricing — Stripe supports it; decide if we bother.
- Before shipping: confirm with user (per CLAUDE.md: "Ask before changing pricing").

**Not in scope yet:**
- Ads (ruled out by free-to-play + one-off framing).
- Subscriptions.
- In-run cosmetics or paid helpers (keep the game's integrity clean).

**Next step:** user picks the free/paid split, then this becomes concrete implementation tasks (entitlements table, Stripe wiring, UI gating, purchase flow).

title: Combine collection: reflect admin item changes (deprecation/removal) with notes
body:
When admins edit, deprecate, or remove items, players' collections (`combine_discoveries`) should reflect those changes cleanly — and the player should get a note when something they collected changes meaningfully.

**Scenarios to handle:**

1. **Item removed / deprecated** (admin deletes or sets `status` away from `live`):
   - Discovery row exists but the item no longer renders.
   - Options:
     - **Soft-retire:** keep the row, render it as "deprecated" with a note ("No longer in Made Of — you discovered it before it was retired").
     - **Hide:** remove from the active collection view, keep in a "legacy" section.
     - **Hard-delete:** cascade erase. Bad — loses player progress. Current `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `combine_discoveries.itemId` makes this the default; see existing memory [Seed wipes Combine discoveries].
   - Recommendation: soft-retire with a visible note. Needs schema: either drop the cascade and add a `retired_at` on the discovery row, or keep an archival snapshot (name, pictogram, tier) alongside the item id.

2. **Item renamed / pictogram changed:**
   - The collection updates naturally (reads from `items`).
   - If the change is substantial (name is meaningfully different), optionally surface a "This item was updated" note on the collection card.

3. **Item moved out of a theme:**
   - Discovery stays (scope is `endless` or `daily`, not per-theme). No action needed except not re-offering it in that theme.

4. **Item split / merged** (future):
   - Split: one discovery becomes two? Flag for admin review rather than auto-split.
   - Merge: two discoveries collapse into one — add a note on the survivor.

**What "with a note" means:**
- On the collection card, a small badge: "Updated" / "Retired" / "Merged."
- Tap → short modal: what changed, when, and (if applicable) the new item it points to.
- Don't spam: only notes for meaningful changes, not every pictogram touch-up.

**Admin side:**
- When deleting/deprecating a live item, the admin UI should warn how many user discoveries point to it.
- Offer options at delete-time: retire-with-note, redirect-to-another-item, or hard-delete (dangerous, confirm).

**Schema implications:**
- Likely want to drop `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `combine_discoveries.itemId` (per existing memory, this was already a source of pain).
- Add nullable fields: `retired_at`, `redirected_to_item_id`, `change_note`.

**Related:**
- [Seed wipes Combine discoveries](memory) — same root cause (cascade on itemId).
- T-0007 (bulk upload draft/review flow) — adjacent "lifecycle of items" concern.
- T-0034 (discovery notifications) — same surface, same "card" treatment.

**Open:**
- Do retired items still count toward partial-completion milestones (T-0008)? Probably yes for everything you earned before retirement, so the milestone doesn't regress.
- Audit trail: do we need an immutable log of every discovery change for support purposes?

title: Content: add "chemical salt" (NaCl) as distinct item from natural salt
body:
We currently only have **natural salt** (geologic/biological source — seawater, rock salt). Add **chemical salt** as a separate item — synthesised NaCl from elements — because their provenance differs.

Shape:
- New item: "chemical salt" (or "synthetic salt" / "NaCl" — pick a name consistent with how other chem items are named).
- Recipe: `Na + Cl → chemical salt`.
- Provenance chain traces back through elemental sodium and chlorine → stars → big bang.
- Natural salt keeps its existing links (seawater `s`, rock `s`, etc.) — no changes.
- Decide theme membership (Everyday? Everything? neither?) and tier.

Why distinct items, not one:
- A single "salt" item would need multi-parent provenance that mixes two totally different origin stories — Made Of's whole point is that the chain is real and sourced. Two items keeps each chain honest.
- Downstream recipes (table salt in food, salt in chemistry) may legitimately point to one source or the other.

Open:
- Should bowtie/explore link them visually as "siblings" / "see also"?
- Are there other items with the same split problem worth auditing in one pass (e.g., water — tap vs distilled? sugar — cane vs synthetic?)? Likely yes, but out of scope for this task — flag follow-up if found.

Related: T-0033 (this was the test case for the mobile recipe editor).

title: Item page bugs: dedupe "Made from" ingredients; fix empty black button under "First appeared"
body:
Two visible bugs on the item page (seen on `nucleotides`):

**1. Duplicate ingredients in "Made from".**
- The list shows carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus — each appears twice.
- Likely cause: nucleotides have multiple recipes (each nucleobase has its own recipe that shares the same ingredients), and the "Made from" view is unioning recipe-scoped `f` links without deduping by target item.
- Fix: dedupe by target item id in the "Made from" roll-up. Keep the per-recipe view separate if we need it elsewhere.
- Audit: check other items with multiple recipes for the same symptom (water, salt, common molecules).

**2. Empty black button under "First appeared / Date not yet known".**
- A large dark rectangle renders with no label, no icon, no obvious action.
- Likely: a button or chip that's missing its text/icon when the data is absent (e.g., "date not yet known" clears the content but the button shell stays).
- Fix: hide the button entirely when there's no first-appeared date; or render a de-emphasized "Add a date" link for admins only.

Where to look:
- "Made from" roll-up: likely in the item page's bowtie or ingredient-list component.
- Empty button: the "First appeared" row near the item header.

Open:
- The duplication may actually be *recipe-aware* data (two recipes = two sets of inputs), in which case the fix is to group them by recipe with a recipe header. Confirm the intended design before deduping blindly.

title: Combine: add spacing between "Keep playing" and "Wipe" helper buttons
body:
"Keep playing" and "Wipe" buttons sit flush against each other — no gap between them. Easy misclick, especially on mobile.

**Context:** "Wipe" is a **helper**, not a progress-wipe — it clears the current board/tray within a run. So the risk is wasting a helper charge, not losing a collection.

Fix:
- Add a visible gap (e.g., `gap-3` / 12–16px) between the two buttons.
- Minor: give Wipe a slightly distinct visual so the two actions don't read as one control, but no confirm dialog needed (it's just a helper).

Where: Combine in-run UI where helpers live (likely the helper tray near the board).

Open:

title: Combine: age progression counts every recipe execution, not unique discoveries (bug)
body:
**Confirmed bug.** Age progression increments on every successful combine, not on unique first-time discoveries at the current age's band.

**Evidence (from a code audit):**

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:481`** — the increment:
  ```ts
  if (recipe.band === state.age + 1 && mult === 1) state.ageMade++;
  ```
  No check against `state.found` — so duplicates count.

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:528, 542`** — the age-up comparison:
  ```ts
  if (state.age < totalAges - 1 && state.ageMade >= ageNeed(state.age, bundle))
  ```

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:293–300`** — the documented intent of `ageNeed`:
  > "Unique discoveries at the current age's band needed to leave each age. Only first-time makes of items whose minimum band is `age + 1` count."
  The comment says unique; the implementation doesn't enforce it.

- **Adjacent state used correctly elsewhere:**
  - `state.found[]` (lines 466–468) already tracks unique item ids via `!state.found.includes(recipe.out)`.
  - `state.madeCounts[recipe.out]` (line 473) is the "repeat makes" counter — distinct from first-finds.

So the fix pattern already exists in the same file for discovery tracking; it just isn't used for `ageMade`.

**Fix:**
- At line 481, only increment when the item is a first-time find at its band:
  ```ts
  if (recipe.band === state.age + 1 && mult === 1 && !state.found.includes(recipe.out))
    state.ageMade++;
  ```
  (Place this before line 466's `found.push`, or hoist the first-find check so both branches share it.)
- Add a unit test: make the same item twice at the current age → `ageMade` goes up by 1, not 2.

**Scope / impact:**
- This has been shipped, so historical runs scored under the lenient (buggier) rule. Decide:
  - (a) Leave historical `progress` rows alone, new rows use the fixed rule — leaderboards will have a soft reset at the fix date.
  - (b) Backfill nothing — data loss risk and we don't have the per-combine log to recompute.
  - Recommended: (a). Note the change in `append_changelog`.

**Related:**
- T-0030 (unique ages scoring bug) — adjacent "unique-vs-not" bug in a different counter. Worth looking at both together.
- T-0005 (serve age chains from server) — tangential, but if we're touching age logic, consider whether the fix has any implications there.
- The `2026-11 bug` note in `src/combine/data.ts` (band collapse when `numAges > uniqueLevels`) is a **separate** issue, not this one.

**Open:**
- Should Fast mode use the same fixed rule? Yes — same engine, same intent.
- Confirm the change doesn't make ages unreachable for small themes / Everyday (fewer unique band items means hitting `ageNeed` is harder). If so, lower `ageNeed` as part of the same change.

comments.body:
**Approach**

- **Fix:** hoist the first-find check so both the discovery branch and the age-progression increment share it. Concretely in `src/combine/engine.ts` around line 466:
  ```ts
  const first = state.mode !== "fast" && !state.found.includes(recipe.out);
  ```
  becomes two signals — the discovery gate (which must stay fast-mode-aware) and the unique-at-band gate for ageMade. Cleanest version: compute `const uniqueFind = !state.found.includes(recipe.out)` before the mutations, keep the `first` definition for discovery event, and change line 481 to:
  ```ts
  if (recipe.band === state.age + 1 && mult === 1 && uniqueFind) state.ageMade++;
  ```
  Order matters: must read `uniqueFind` BEFORE `state.found.push(recipe.out)` on line 468.

- **Fast mode:** Fast skips `found.push` entirely (see line 466 — gated on `state.mode !== "fast"`), so under the current implementation every craft in Fast is "not in found". If we naively use `!state.found.includes`, Fast would age up on dupes too (same bug just via a different path). **Decision:** Fast mode runs are short (2-part only, no bands) — need to verify Fast actually hits the age-up path at all. Looking at engine behavior now.

- **Test:** add to `tests/` — simulate: same single-band item crafted twice at age 0 → `state.ageMade === 1`. Also: two different band items → `ageMade === 2`.

- **Reachability sanity check:** inspect `ageNeed` for Everyday + Everything themes after the fix. If any band's `bandSize * UNLOCK_FRACTION` floors below `baselineNeed`, we're fine. If it climbs above the number of unique items in the band, ages become unreachable — would need a cap at `bandSize(age, bundle)`.

- **History:** No backfill. Note the soft leaderboard reset in changelog.

**Files I'll touch:**
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — the fix (and verify fast mode behavior)
- `tests/combine-engine.test.ts` (or nearest existing engine test) — new test cases

**Landed**

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:466-486`** — hoisted `uniqueFind = !state.found.includes(recipe.out)` above the mutations; gated `state.ageMade++` on `(state.mode === "fast" || uniqueFind)`. Updated the inline comment block to explain the new contract.
- **`src/combine/__tests__/engine.test.ts`** — added `describe("ageMade counts only unique on-band first-finds (T-0051)")` with 3 cases:
  - re-making the same on-band item doesn't bump `ageMade`
  - two different on-band items each bump it
  - fast mode keeps counting repeats (its `ageMade` is just a termination signal, not real progression — Fast skips `found.push` so a naive `uniqueFind` check would make Fast runs never terminate via `ageMade`)

**Test results:** 84 passed / 2 failed in engine.test.ts. The 2 failures are pre-existing hold-zone tests that fail on `main` before my change (confirmed via `git stash`) — unrelated.

**Typecheck:** clean. Full suite: 293 passed / 2 failed (same pre-existing failures).

**Didn't do:**
- No `progress` backfill — noted the soft leaderboard reset in changelog.
- Didn't lower `ageNeed`: reachability sanity check — `ageNeed = max(baselineNeed(age), round(bandSize * 0.4))` is always `<= bandSize` for the realistic case (0.4 ≤ 1), and `baselineNeed(age) = 7 + 2*age` is unlikely to exceed `bandSize` for Everything's authored ages. Everyday has fewer items per band but still comfortably above 7 for age 0. If a small theme bumps this later, we'll see it as an unreachable-age bug and can cap at `bandSize(age, bundle)` in `ageNeed`.
- The 2 pre-existing hold-zone failures: tracked separately, not T-0051 scope.
